question: why did the mask collapse after 09-03? (DA 304 / REVIEW)
VERDICT: NOT DETERMINABLE FROM WHAT WAS COLLECTED
consequence: no exclusion of 09-01..09-03 is licensed, so 0.636 remains the planning rate and 0.875 the optimistic bound, in that order

FIRST_THE_PREMISE_IS_CORRECTED.what_was_reported: a step change in WINDOW SUPPLY -- 247-265 windows on 09-01..09-03 against 284 on 09-11
FIRST_THE_PREMISE_IS_CORRECTED.what_is_true: window SUPPLY is FLAT at 288 files/day for btc AND eth on every day 09-01..09-11. The archive never varied.
FIRST_THE_PREMISE_IS_CORRECTED.what_247_265_actually_is: the count of windows with PRESENT content. The difference is EMPTY SHELLS, not missing files: btc carried 22 shells on 09-01, 40 on 09-02, 39 on 09-03, then 0,0,0,1,0,0,0 and 3 on 09-11.
FIRST_THE_PREMISE_IS_CORRECTED.why_it_matters: supply and content are different quantities with different causes. A supply break would point at the market or the subscription list; a content break points at the feed. Only the second happened.

CONDITIONS_TESTED_AND_RULED_OUT.collector_version: clob_v4_1 on EVERY day 09-01..09-12. No version change at the boundary.
CONDITIONS_TESTED_AND_RULED_OUT.window_supply: 288/day both coins, every day. No change.
CONDITIONS_TESTED_AND_RULED_OUT.collector_process_restart: NONE since 09-01 -- the msgs counter never goes backwards. The process that produced the shells is the same process that stopped producing them.
CONDITIONS_TESTED_AND_RULED_OUT.markets_tracked: monotone growth 168 -> 22,343, ~2,016/day, with no break at 09-03/04.
CONDITIONS_TESTED_AND_RULED_OUT.collector_code: the only commits are 2026-09-01T02:16 and 02:23 (restoring deployed collector bytes). They PRECEDE the shell-heavy days rather than ending them.
CONDITIONS_TESTED_AND_RULED_OUT.unit_configuration: pm-collector-clob.service.d and v41.conf last modified 2026-08-31T21:50 -- again before, not at, the boundary.
CONDITIONS_TESTED_AND_RULED_OUT.host_event: no reboot: continuously up since 2026-08-26T04:37:59Z. And journald had vacuumed anything from that period, so system-level evidence does not exist to test.

THE_ONE_NEARBY_CONDITION_AND_WHY_IT_IS_N: a collector deploy/restore landed 2026-09-01T02:16-02:23, immediately before the three shell-heavy days. That is a real condition, independently evidenced by git log and unit mtimes, and it does not identify the days by outcome. BUT IT EXPLAINS THE WRONG END: it precedes the shell period and says nothing about why shells STOPPED on 09-04. Nothing found explains the STOP, and a condition that accounts for the start while leaving the end unexplained is not a licence to exclude the days.

WHY_THIS_IS_NOT_ONE_OF_THE_THREE_ILLEGIT.not_(i)_no_condition_named: conditions were named and TESTED -- version, supply, restart, code, unit, host -- and each was ruled out on its own evidence rather than left unexamined
WHY_THIS_IS_NOT_ONE_OF_THE_THREE_ILLEGIT.not_(ii)_supported_by_the_outcomes: every quantity checked is recorded continuously and independently of whether a day passed: version strings, file counts, a monotone message counter, commit timestamps, file mtimes
WHY_THIS_IS_NOT_ONE_OF_THE_THREE_ILLEGIT.not_(iii)_identifies_days_by_outcome: no condition was found at all, so none is proposed; the days are not being identified by anything

WHAT_WOULD_DETERMINE_IT: journald retention covering 09-01..09-03, which was vacuumed
a collector-side counter for subscription churn or resubscribe events, which is not recorded
the venue's own status history for that period, which is not collected
THE_SHELLS_AND_THE_STALLS_ARE_THE_SAME_P: all-coin zero-rate minutes per day run 72/29/35 on 09-01..09-03, ZERO on 09-04..09-10, and 23 on 09-11 -- the same shape as the shell counts. So there is ONE mechanism across the whole period, not a 09-01..09-03 regime and a separate 09-11 event.
